title: Spiking Neural Networks for Image Classification and Recognition
content: Spiking neural networks (SNNs) constitute the third generation of neural computational models, replacing the continuous-valued activations of conventional artificial neural networks (ANNs) with discrete, asynchronous spike events that more closely resemble the dynamics of biological neurons. By encoding information in the timing and sparsity of spikes, SNNs promise substantial reductions in energy consumption when deployed on event-driven neuromorphic hardware, making them attractive for image classification and recognition on resource-constrained platforms. This paper presents a deep SNN image classifier built from leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF) neurons and trained end to end with surrogate-gradient backpropagation through time. We review the foundations of spiking computation, learning rules ranging from spike-timing-dependent plasticity to direct surrogate-gradient training and ANN-to-SNN conversion, and recent spiking transformer architectures. We then formalize the membrane-potential dynamics and the surrogate-gradient estimator used to train the network, and describe the complete training procedure as an algorithm. On standard static benchmarks (CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, ImageNet) and a neuromorphic dataset, our framework is intended to deliver competitive accuracy at low inference latency and low estimated energy. We conclude by outlining open challenges in scaling directly-trained SNNs and co-designing them with neuromorphic accelerators.
